question: What release cadence should this repository run on, and how should out-of-band (mid-week urgent) releases be authorized?
options: Weekly wave, America/Los_Angeles: Monday-Friday is the merge window (closes end of Friday), Saturday is release day (one release PR rolls up pending changesets, owner approves the publish batch once), Sunday is consumer-adoption day, Monday starts fresh. Regular semver (patch/minor/major by changeset level) -- no week-numbered version. A package or week with no pending changesets releases nothing. Out-of-band releases are for security fixes or a broken published release only, as an owner-approved patch (later widened -- see decision below).
CalVer scheme YY.WW.N (ISO week-year/week plus a same-week counter), or 0.YYWW.N (the same, kept pre-1.0).
No fixed cadence; release whenever a change lands.
recommendation: Option 1 (weekly wave, regular semver, owner-approved out-of-band); CalVer considered and rejected during PR #1316's own drafting, per that PR's own account of two owner-directed revisions.
decision: The owner set the calendar directly in a standing-rule comment (#1187 comment 5799538912, 'Standing rule: weekly release calendar (owner direction, 2026-09-23)'): Monday-Friday merge window (closes end of Friday, America/Los_Angeles), Saturday release (one release PR, one owner approval of the publish batch), Sunday consumer adoption (one grouped @clossys/* update PR per consuming repository, a Controller CI convention), Monday starts fresh; regular semver driven by changeset levels, not week-numbered versions; a package with no pending changesets is not released that week, and a week with no changesets anywhere opens no release PR. That same comment states out-of-band releases are for security fixes or a broken published release only, as an owner-approved patch. A follow-up owner comment (#1187 comment 5800369031, item 2) widened this: the owner may approve an out-of-band release on any day to clear an urgent update, not only a security fix or a broken release, and only the owner ever applies the release:out-of-band label. The specific mechanics for that widened scope -- patch stays the default, a minor out-of-band bump needs the changeset to also carry owner-approved: minor, and major is never allowed out of band -- are PR #1316's own 'Follow-up owner decision' drafting, not a separate #1187 comment; the PR's own body states this was itself one of two revisions 'by owner decision'. The owner then signed off on the implementation PR directly: 'Owner sign-off: the owner approved this weekly release calendar (Friday merge cut-off, Saturday release, Sunday consumer adoption, with ad hoc mid-week owner approvals for urgent updates) on 2026-09-23, at head 348e385b, after independent APPROVE (Opus) and RECOMMEND ACCEPT (second reviewer) at that head' (https://github.com/clossys/foundry/pull/1316#issuecomment-5801304853). This record's own `links.patchIds` pins `git patch-id --stable` of PR #1316's net diff against its merge base (its base ref, `claude/release-batching`, not `main`) at head 348e385b, computed and verified directly against that merge base rather than assumed -- NOT a head sha: this very record landing (as part of this repository's HITL first-slice work) advances `main`, which is exactly what forces PR #1316 into a `BEHIND` state and a restack once this record is committed, changing its head sha. A head-sha pin would break at that exact moment; the patch-id does not, because restacking does not change the content of the diff being hashed. PR #1316 lands through the merge train AFTER that restack, at whatever new head sha it then carries, because `scripts/land-stack.mjs`'s tier-2 gate recomputes the patch-id fresh at merge time and finds it still matches this record's `links.patchIds` -- it is the patch-id, not the head sha, that is understood to carry this sign-off forward.
